machine: M1 Pro (aarch64 macOS), 10 cores, shared with other build jobs
reproduce: cargo run --release -p axil-decide --example u1_bench -- --threads N --out FILE.json; cargo test --release -p axil-decide --test u1_parity -- --ignored

parity.note: Rust and Python onnxruntime 1.22.0 produce the same float32 logits; the residual is float64 rounding in the calibration.

batched_fp32_check.model: onnx/model.onnx (fp32) of the same revision, batch-invariant
batched_fp32_check.note: The int8 model is not batch-invariant (one activation scale per batch tensor), so the runtime scores it one pair per call; batching it moved probabilities by up to 0.27 in Python.

latency.what: one pair per call (tokenize + run + calibrate), 249 U1 pairs; Rust after 5 warm-up pairs, Python without; load = session creation (+ tokenizer for Rust), first in process; one run each, Rust then Python per thread count
latency.caveat: Measured while other jobs saturated the machine, so these are upper bounds and the Rust/Python gap is mostly the load changing between runs. The bake-off measured Python p50 19.3 ms (4 threads) on a quieter machine (typed-decisions-bakeoff-2026-09-27.json). Re-measure on an idle machine and on x86 Linux before choosing where the model runs.
